items.title: Billy Taylor — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I knew Randy would love it because when we were both recording for Riverside records... we talked about them a lot... So we both gravitated… we used to talk about these things

ctx.x: Les Paul and Mary Ford who had sold a lot of records for them. So they had a lot of big record sellers on the label. None of them could get their records pressed. They pressed nothing but Beatles. Now here I am with a turntable hit. I mean I am playing on WNEW and everybody in the middle of the road station of which there were many in those days was playing… whatever we were playing they played. So all over the country my records are being heard. Nowhere in the country can they buy them because they are not being…

I was having a ball with records. I was hearing everything and my playing was growing by leaps and bounds because I was listening to stuff that I wouldn’t have listened to otherwise and it really was affecting my playing. I mean you would hear it my work. So my love for Latin music… I was able to do whole shows of the Latin influence and do Macheto and do all the guys that I like. So all of this stuff is going on and I had determined that Beatles or not, if the records thing goes on it’s face, I mean I have got…
